Hi Leah — thanks for the clear list. Answering inline for brevity; attaching our data lifecycle summary and SOC2 extract.

1) Geographic storage:
- Primary: Customer request payloads and derived tokens are stored in the region you select during provisioning (we currently support us-west-2 and eu-west-1 for hosted accounts).
- Region guarantees: For hosted API customers who select a region, we keep data at-rest and in transit within that region under normal operation (including KV cache and persisted logs). We do not perform cross-region analytics on raw customer payloads.

2) Retention windows (typical defaults):
- Request logs (metadata): 90 days by default; can be reduced to 30 days with an enterprise configuration.
- Model inputs/outputs: Ephemeral by default — kept for up to 7 days for quality monitoring and debugging unless a customer opts in for longer retention.
- Audit traces and billing events: 365 days (immutable for accounting).
- Note: All retention windows are configurable per-tenant via the account settings and can be set in your onboarding document.

3) Deletion workflow:
- Initiation: Customer files a deletion request via the Console (Admin > Data > Request Erasure) or opens a ticket with Support referencing the account id.
- Ownership: Support/Operations owns the request and coordinates with Infra for any infra-level actions.
- Timeline: Standard hosted account erasure (ephemeral and persisted inputs/outputs) completes within 48 hours from request acceptance; logs and billing artifacts follow the configured retention policy (billing/audit records retained per policy unless legal hold).
- Verification: We provide a deletion report (email + Console entry). For enterprise customers we can provide an attestation PDF signed by our Compliance team.

4) Backups and replication:
- Backups: We take encrypted backups for disaster recovery which are region-scoped by default. Where we run cross-region replication (only for customers who elected geo-redundancy), backups are replicated to the selected DR region.
- Deletion across replicas: Deletion requests trigger an orchestration workflow that enumerates replicas and issues coordinated deletes. For replicated accounts, full replication deletion timelines may extend up to 72 hours to ensure consistency across storage tiers.

If you need exact SLAs for the Lyricon environment (non-replication vs geo-redundant), tell me the preference and I can provide the explicit timeline we'd commit in the contract.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Thanks Ben — quick responses:
- Attestation: We can provide a signed deletion attestation for enterprise deals. Standard attestation includes deletion timeline, scope (objects deleted), and operator runbook reference.
- Addendum for geo-redundancy: Yes — we add a small addendum spelling out extended timelines and DR replication handling; this does not change the baseline retention defaults but documents the replication behavior.
- Ops constraints: 48 hours for standard hosted erasure (non-replicated) is achievable. For replicated accounts, 72 hours is conservative but realistic because of snapshots and tape-retention windows in some provider regions. We should avoid promising under 48 hours.

I'll draft the attestation wording and the geo-redundancy addendum; Mina, want me to send that directly to Leah or to you for initial review?
